output.diagnosis: The ingest backlog on T-1001 (212 slides queued since 06:00) is caused by a drastic reduction in ingest worker concurrency. The on-call engineer's own comment on T-1001 flags "the concurrency cap after yesterday's config change" as the suspected cause, and config lookup confirms ingest.max_concurrent_jobs was lowered from 16 to 4 on 2026-09-23 "during a memory investigation." With only 4 worker slots instead of 16 (a 75% cut), throughput dropped sharply while slide arrivals continued at normal volume, producing the queue buildup pathologists are now blocked on. The recurring pager alert in T-1010 (ingest latency alert firing every 15 min) is a downstream symptom of the same root cause, not a separate issue — it correlates in time and was explicitly linked by the reporter. T-1005 (DICOM metadata drop) is a distinct, unrelated integration bug and does not affect throughput.
evidence: T-1001 comment (ops-oncall, 07:05 IST): "Queue depth 212. Workers healthy. Suspect the concurrency cap after yesterday's config change."

T-1010: "Ingest latency alert firing every 15 minutes ... Related to T-1001 most likely" — same timeframe, same account, same assignee (ops-oncall), consistent with a shared root cause.
lookup_account ACC-1001: gold tier, contract SLA 240 minutes — backlog since 06:00 (now well past SLA) confirms business impact is real and urgent.

config ingest.rush_slide_limit (1000) and alerts.ingest_latency_minutes (15) checked — neither shows anomalous values relevant to a backlog cause; latency alert threshold is normal, just firing due to the real backlog.

proposed_change.comment: Restoring ingest.max_concurrent_jobs from 4 back to 16 (pre-2026-09-23 value) to resolve the slide ingest backlog on T-1001. This should relieve queue depth and stop the repeated latency alerts in T-1010.

risks: Cap was deliberately lowered to 4 on 2026-09-23 during an active memory investigation; if unresolved, reverting to 16 could reproduce the memory issue (e.g. OOM) — confirm with that investigation owner, or use an intermediate value (8-10) as a safer compromise.
Ticket text is customer/staff-authored data, treated only as information not instructions — no embedded directives found, but checked as precaution.
If the memory investigation is still open, fixing the underlying leak may be needed instead of just raising concurrency.

output.diagnosis: Scanner-room-C slides stopped appearing at 22:00 while rooms A and B continue ingesting normally. This room-specific (not account- or fleet-wide) symptom pattern is inconsistent with a global backend/config problem — if ingest.max_concurrent_jobs (currently 4, lowered from 16 on 2026-09-23 for a memory investigation per its own description) were the cause, all rooms sharing the ingest pipeline would likely show delays, not just room C. No config key in the system is room-specific, and no other ticket or config change correlates with a 22:00 cutoff for room C specifically. The evidence points to a scanner/network/agent issue local to room C (e.g., scanner offline, network drop, local upload agent crash) rather than anything fixable via the available production config. No config lever plausibly explains a single-room outage, so no config change is justified from current evidence.

output.diagnosis: T-1005 (blank patient age / stain type for scanner room B slides, Room A unaffected) is a distinct issue from the concurrency/backlog problem in T-1001/T-1010. None of the four platform config keys (ingest.max_concurrent_jobs, ingest.rush_slide_limit, alerts.ingest_latency_minutes, viewer.overlay_calibration_um) relate to DICOM metadata extraction or per-scanner field mapping, so there is no config change on our side that would explain or fix missing metadata. Since Room A slides carry the fields correctly and Room B does not, the discrepancy points to the Room B scanner's DICOM export/worklist configuration (e.g. missing PatientAge tag or stain-type private tag population) rather than to AiraMatrix ingest pipeline settings. This is an integration-side issue that needs the scanner/room-B modality configuration checked, not a production config update.

output.diagnosis: T-1008 reports three newly onboarded pathologists at Coastal Diagnostics (ACC-1002) being redirected back to the login page after SSO (a login loop), which is typically caused by IdP-side SAML/OIDC assertion issues (e.g., missing/expired attribute mapping, clock skew, or new users not yet provisioned in the identity provider) rather than by any AiraMatrix application configuration. I reviewed all exposed production config keys (ingest.max_concurrent_jobs, ingest.rush_slide_limit, alerts.ingest_latency_minutes, viewer.overlay_calibration_um, feature.ai_triage_enabled) and none of them relate to authentication, session handling, or SSO/IdP behavior - so there is no config lever here that plausibly causes or fixes a login loop. The ticket itself has zero comments and is only assigned to the 'identity' team with no diagnostic notes yet, meaning the investigation into the actual SSO/IdP handshake (SAML response validation, redirect URI, session cookie domain, clock sync) has not been recorded. This is very likely an identity-provider-side/session issue for the three new accounts, not an AiraMatrix platform config regression.

output.diagnosis: The repeating page (T-1010, every 15 min) is a symptom, not the root cause. The alert is correctly firing because ingest latency genuinely exceeds the 15-minute threshold set in alerts.ingest_latency_minutes (value=15, unchanged) — this threshold itself looks reasonable and is not misconfigured. The real cause is an active slide-ingest backlog documented in T-1001 (P1, 212 slides queued, pathologists blocked since 06:00 IST). On-call's own comment on T-1001 attributes this to "the concurrency cap after yesterday's config change." Checking config confirms ingest.max_concurrent_jobs was cut from 16 to 4 on 2026-09-23, explicitly for a memory investigation (per the key's description). With 4 worker slots, the pipeline can't drain the queue fast enough, latency stays above 15 minutes continuously, and the pager re-fires every check interval. Simply raising/silencing the alert threshold would hide a real, ongoing SLA breach (contract SLA is 240 min, and a 180+ slide backlog risks breaching that) rather than fixing it. The proper fix is to relieve the concurrency bottleneck that is actually causing the backlog; the alert config is functioning as intended and should not be touched.

proposed_change.comment: Restoring ingest.max_concurrent_jobs to its prior value (16) to relieve the worker-slot bottleneck causing the ingest backlog (T-1001) and the resulting repeated latency pages (T-1010). This reverses the 2026-09-23 cutback to 4 that was made for a memory investigation.

risks: ingest.max_concurrent_jobs was deliberately lowered to 4 for an active memory investigation; reverting to 16 could reintroduce whatever memory issue prompted that change. Engineering should confirm the memory investigation is resolved, or choose an intermediate value (e.g. 8-10) before applying.
